estimand_or_target: Descriptive mean, median, dispersion and missingness
breast_cancer_example: Summarize a synthetic continuous tumor marker at diagnosis
interpretation: Report median/IQR or mean/SD with observed n; no hypothesis p-value
common_pitfall: A mean of specimen ID or a descriptive p-value is meaningless

breast_cancer_example: Count synthetic ER-positive and ER-negative receptor reports
interpretation: State numerator/denominator and missing cases separately
common_pitfall: Numerically coded receptor status is not continuous

breast_cancer_example: Summarize repeated tumor scores without counting visits as independent people
interpretation: Separate n patients and n specimens before summaries
common_pitfall: A row-level SD may represent within-person rather than between-person variation

breast_cancer_example: Estimate weighted breast-screening prevalence from a probability survey
interpretation: Use design-aware interval estimates, not naive row-level SE
common_pitfall: Weights alone without PSUs and strata may misstate uncertainty

breast_cancer_example: Compare serial synthetic biomarker trajectories during therapy
interpretation: Define cluster-specific vs marginal estimand and correlation-aware SE
common_pitfall: Repeated measurements are not independent patients

estimand_or_target: Gene-level log fold changes with FDR
breast_cancer_example: Contrast synthetic ESR1/ERBB2-related expression profiles with biological replicates
interpretation: Report log2-fold changes and a defined multiplicity family
common_pitfall: Do not run raw-count models on log-transformed data or technical cells as biological replicates

breast_cancer_example: Predict a synthetic recurrence indicator from baseline markers
interpretation: Report held-out discrimination, calibration and uncertainty
common_pitfall: A low training error is not independent validation or causal inference

estimand_or_target: Adjusted predictor association at prespecified covariates
breast_cancer_example: Adjust treatment and stage in a hypothetical response analysis
interpretation: Report adjusted effect and CI on an outcome-appropriate scale
common_pitfall: Covariate adjustment alone does not guarantee causal identification

estimand_or_target: Survival function or adjusted hazard over defined follow-up
breast_cancer_example: Compare synthetic recurrence-free time between two treatment arms
interpretation: Report KM probabilities or HR with time horizon and censoring caveats
common_pitfall: HR is not a risk ratio; deaths may compete with recurrence

estimand_or_target: Define at-risk population before time-to-event inference
breast_cancer_example: Specify surgery-to-first-recurrence time zero for a synthetic cohort
interpretation: Record unambiguous origin, event status, risk set and competing events
common_pitfall: Do not fit survival model with undefined follow-up origin

breast_cancer_example: Count synthetic emergency visits by cancer treatment and person-years
interpretation: Exponentiated log-link coefficient is an event-rate ratio
common_pitfall: Ignoring exposure and overdispersion misstates count-model inference

estimand_or_target: Audit exposure denominator before rate modeling
breast_cancer_example: Check duration of each woman's synthetic oncology follow-up
interpretation: Establish event window and exposure units before Poisson regression
common_pitfall: Number of people does not equal person-years when follow-up differs

breast_cancer_example: Study association between age and synthetic baseline biomarker
interpretation: Correlation is not a slope and neither proves causality
common_pitfall: A correlation of repeated specimens violates ordinary independent SE

breast_cancer_example: Measure tumor marker before and after treatment in the same women
interpretation: Report mean paired change and CI in assay units
common_pitfall: Independent-group t tests discard pairing and may alter uncertainty

estimand_or_target: Asymmetry in paired binary status changes
breast_cancer_example: Test paired ER-status transitions in the same women
interpretation: Report negative-to-positive and positive-to-negative discordant counts
common_pitfall: A cross-sectional chi-square ignores matched observations

breast_cancer_example: Compare synthetic paired toxicity grades before and after treatment
interpretation: Signed-rank location claims need assumptions about difference symmetry
common_pitfall: A rank test does not automatically measure the change in means

estimand_or_target: Pair-aware analysis beyond simple two-visit tests
breast_cancer_example: Three repeated biopsies per woman with missing visits
interpretation: Require model that handles visit timing and patient dependence
common_pitfall: Do not apply simple paired t test to three visits

breast_cancer_example: Clarify whether synthetic treatment has one, two or three arms
interpretation: State comparison labels before choosing a test family
common_pitfall: Do not auto-select t versus ANOVA without groups

estimand_or_target: Difference in two independent population means
breast_cancer_example: Compare hypothetical biomarker means between two patient arms
interpretation: Report A-minus-B mean difference and Welch CI; zero in CI is not equality
common_pitfall: Welch does not correct pseudoreplication or confounding

estimand_or_target: Omnibus inequality of three or more means
breast_cancer_example: Compare three independent synthetic breast-cancer marker groups
interpretation: An omnibus rejection means at least one population mean differs
common_pitfall: Do not attach ordinary Tukey intervals to Welch ANOVA

estimand_or_target: Specify one-sample or multigroup continuous contrast
breast_cancer_example: Choose one-sample reference versus between-arm biomarker question
interpretation: Declare mean benchmark or treatment contrasts first
common_pitfall: A one-sample t test requires an externally justified reference

breast_cancer_example: Test invented toxicity grade frequencies against a prespecified reference
interpretation: Report grade proportions and exact/asymptotic distribution fit
common_pitfall: An ordered one-sample outcome is not a two-sample rank contrast

breast_cancer_example: Compare synthetic toxicity grades in independent cohorts
interpretation: Report rank/distribution contrast; not automatically median difference
common_pitfall: Differences in shape can prevent median-only interpretation

breast_cancer_example: Compare ordinal adverse-event grades across three regimens
interpretation: An omnibus rank difference does not identify which arm or median differs
common_pitfall: Unplanned pairwise analyses need multiplicity control

breast_cancer_example: Compare invented subtype counts to an external reference distribution
interpretation: Assess whole-category fit with expected cell counts
common_pitfall: Reference proportions fitted from same data change the null distribution

estimand_or_target: One success probability versus fixed benchmark
breast_cancer_example: Assess 36 response events among 80 eligible synthetic patients vs p0=.35
interpretation: Report response fraction, exact tail and interval with sidedness
common_pitfall: A historical p0 alone is not a treatment counterfactual

breast_cancer_example: Assess synthetic HER2-status versus documented response table
interpretation: Report raw counts, row denominators and suitable risk or odds measure
common_pitfall: Chi-square p alone gives no effect size; exact choice depends on design
